items.q: Can you replace our existing pretreatment?
items.a: Yes, on makes and equipment confirmed when you enquire. We assess the system and replace the train; the existing pretreatment runs until cutover.

items.q: Our water meets drinking water standards. Why is that not enough?
items.a: Those standards protect people, not membranes. Health Canada sets no guideline value for chloramine; the US EPA allows up to 4 mg/L. Polyamide reverse osmosis membranes typically tolerate < 0.1 mg/L of free chlorine.
It is priced per project, for a train sized to your demand.

items.q: How do you show the design covers seasonal changes?
items.a: In the design basis, month by month. We take the history you have of utility and site data and size every bed for each parameter's worst month, before you order.

items.q: Is pretreatment part of the validated system?
items.a: Not necessarily: your risk assessment sets the boundary; write it into your user requirement specification (URS). WHO TRS 1033 allows construction to drinking water standards up to the reverse osmosis stage. Either way, the turnover package covers pretreatment, with installation and operational qualification where in scope.

items.q: What is replaced, and how often?
items.a: Five items, set from your feed water: cartridges, filter media, carbon, softener resin and salt. Cartridges, media and resin follow intervals set for your system; salt follows hardness. Carbon follows an interval set for your system, reset from your microbial counts. It is replaced, not hot-water sanitized: PVC is rated to 60 °C, at 22 % of its pressure rating.

items.q: What is the pretreatment built from?
items.a: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe to the standard and schedule named in your proposal, joined by the method named there. It stays upstream of the reverse osmosis stage, so it never touches Purified Water. Vessels: material named in your proposal.

items.q: What happens to the ammonia from chloramine?
items.a: Some passes the reverse osmosis membranes as ammonia gas, at the pH used to control CO₂. It then loads the electrodeionization stage, so we design chloramine removal and the Purified Water skid together.
